cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Raise the Stakes
cards.instruction: Persuade them to accept a larger risk, cost, or commitment so the outcome will feel decisive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Let's make this chess game decide who cooks all weekend.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We were playing for a biscuit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Neither of us has been emotionally changed by the biscuit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I don't need chess to change me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you'll enjoy discovering how much the kitchen matters.

mechanism: A controls which terms are worthy of proceeding and permits concessions only when the contest still carries a materially larger consequence than the original stake.
confusable: D197 enforces an agreed cost after outcome; D200 tries to secure a larger commitment beforehand so the future outcome matters.
comparison: Chess biscuit stake grows into household cooking despite schedule constraints; club rematch stakes affect roles and continued participation instead of forgettable pride.
seedUse: Both exact cards and four canonical seeds read. Preserve the larger-risk persuasion and B reluctance, making A terms respond rather than merely proclaiming intensity.
